pairs.subject: app-shell
pairs.evidence: src/features/shared/chrome/sidebar/sections/PluginsSidebarNav.tsx:120 Only top-level sections are registry-derived; the plugin sub-nav ids are hand-kept arrays cast into the tab unions (lines 120-122), which already once shipped a blank page (sidebarData.ts:161-164), so the sub-destination vocabulary still has no single authority.

techniques.evidence: src/features/shared/chrome/sidebar/sections/PluginsSidebarNav.tsx:120 Sub-destination ids are untyped strings cast to DevToolsTab/ObsidianBrainTab/TwinTab; the registry covers only level one. Still unfixed.

src/features/shared/chrome/sidebar/SidebarLevel1.tsx:200 The rail runs an inline tier/dev check, while the palette (commandPaletteUtils.ts:26) and the footer use passesGates. Every gated entry is hidden; nothing is shown locked.

src/features/shared/chrome/sidebar/BadgeSlot.tsx:92 The slot is priority-ranked with a +N overflow, a tooltip listing every signal, and a 99+ cap. But two count badges render side by side on one entry, which the one-slot rule names as layout noise. PluginsSidebarNav also hand-rolls its own pulsing pill (line 133).

src/features/shared/chrome/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx:227 Posture is persisted (Sidebar.tsx:26 localStorage). But when the rail is collapsed, the whole level 2 disappears with no flyout, so sub-destinations exist in one posture only. The L1 name reveal is a native title= (SidebarLevel1.tsx:240).
src/features/shared/chrome/sidebar/SidebarLevel1.tsx:232 Hovering or focusing a rail entry prefetches that section's chunk; it is cancelled on leave or blur.

src/features/shared/chrome/BackgroundServices.tsx:51 One lazy, render-nothing host lists its residents, and each states why it is session-wide or cross-section. Start order is not written down as dependencies; the reaper was not checked.

src/features/shared/chrome/sidebar/SidebarLevel2.tsx:253 The shell imports each screen's sidebar content (persona lists, team lists) and switches on sidebarSection (line 172), which is a shell-side table of which screens have sections. Screens do not portal and register.

pairs.subject: app-shell
pairs.evidence: src/features/plugins/obsidian-brain/ObsidianBrainPage.tsx:10 Six Obsidian panels are split with plain React lazy() (lines 10-15) instead of the lazyRetry wrapper that sibling TwinPage uses, so a transient chunk failure is never retried and lands straight in the ErrorBoundary.

techniques.evidence: src/features/plugins/obsidian-brain/ObsidianBrainPage.tsx:10 No automatic retry before showing the failure. TwinPage.tsx:19-24 uses lazyRetry. Still unfixed.
src/features/plugins/twin/TwinPage.tsx:37 Retired Twin tab ids read back from storage are mapped to live destinations, not rendered blank: the remove-with-fallback rule.

src/features/plugins/obsidian-brain/useObsidianVaultRehydration.ts:29 Vault rehydration is admitted to the shell host on cross-section reach, runs once per session, retries with backoff (RETRY_DELAYS_MS), and has a cancel flag.

pairs.subject: app-shell
pairs.evidence: src/features/overview/components/dashboard/OverviewPage.tsx:63 Each Overview tab switch re-keys the subtree under AnimatePresence, so a warm return re-runs the entrance animation and remounts the tab. Separately, line 73 renders IncidentsInbox with no tier check, so programmatic doors (ProactiveCard.tsx:56 setOverviewTab('incidents')) reach a tab the sidebar hides below TEAM.

techniques.evidence: src/features/overview/components/dashboard/OverviewPage.tsx:73 sidebarData.ts:81 gates Incidents at TEAM only in the sidebar, and overviewSlice.ts:288 setOverviewTab writes without a check, so the destination never consults the gate. Still unfixed.

src/features/overview/components/dashboard/OverviewPage.tsx:63 Chunks use lazyRetry (line 14), which is good. But re-keying with the pageTransition variants replays cold-load choreography on every return, which prohibition 5 names.
src/features/overview/components/dashboard/OverviewPage.tsx:82 An unknown overviewTab falls back to the dashboard rather than a blank viewport.

pairs.subject: app-shell
pairs.evidence: src/features/agents/sub_editor/components/EditorLazyTabs.tsx:3 The editor's Activity/Settings/Lab/Design tabs are split with raw React lazy() and no retry, so a transient chunk failure is not retried. Its tier gate also exists twice: tabDefs minTier in the bar, and a hand-copied isStarter check at the destination.

techniques.evidence: src/features/agents/sub_editor/components/EditorLazyTabs.tsx:3 Raw lazy instead of the repo's lazyRetry, so there is no automatic retry before the failure surfaces.

src/features/agents/sub_editor/components/EditorBody.tsx:126 The destination re-checks with a hand-copied constant, not the declared tabDefs minTier (EditorTabBar.tsx:16,18), and redirects with no explanation (a silent eviction).

src/features/agents/sub_editor/components/EditorTabBar.tsx:104 The active tab is derived from the one store value; legacy ids are remapped (EditorBody.tsx:121). The EditorTab vocabulary is still outside the registry.
src/features/agents/sub_editor/components/EditorTabBar.tsx:124 The tab badge is derived from failedTabs state and carries a screen-reader text equivalent, not just colour.

declined.reason: withdrawn after review: reviewer (sonnet): The evidence says the default tier is TEAM, but uiModes.ts:46-47 defaults BUILD_MAX_TIER to BUILDER, so Welcome and the rail only disagree on TEAM-capped builds; the hand-copied DEV_MODE_SECTIONS set at NavigationGrid.tsx:68 is real, but the stated disagreement does not happen by default.
